title: Holiday Returns Without the Headache: A Simple Returns Policy Guide for Online Stores

linkedin.post:
Holiday returns land in January, when your team is tired and your cash is tight.

Gifts come back more often than anything a shopper buys for themselves. The buyer is not the one who wears the size or picks the color. So guesses turn into returns, and the returns pile up after the sale ends.

The good news is that most of this is avoidable. Here are four fixes that make returns smaller and faster to handle:

1️⃣ Write the policy in plain words
Shoppers read your returns page before they buy. If it is confusing, they choose a store that is clear. Keep it short enough to read in one minute. Include the return window, the eligible items, and who pays for return shipping.

2️⃣ Set a return window your team can handle
Decide how many days a buyer has, and when that clock starts. The delivery date or the ship date both work, as long as the shopper and your staff agree on it. A clear window means fewer messages and fewer surprises in January.

3️⃣ Fix the product pages that cause most returns
Wrong size, wrong color, and vague details send gifts back. Clear photos, sizing notes, and honest descriptions stop many of these returns before the order is placed. Look at last January's returns and check which product pages they came from.

4️⃣ Offer a second option before the refund
A refund does not have to end the sale. Some shoppers would rather exchange the item or take store credit than wait for money to come back. Offering those choices keeps revenue in your store and keeps the customer coming back.

Holiday returns are a sales problem as well as a cost. Plain words, a clear window, and honest product pages cut most of the avoidable ones. Fix them before the rush, not in January.

How many of your December returns came from a product page that could have been clearer?
